task_context.problem_statement: If $x$ and $y$ are positive real numbers such that $5x^2 + 10xy = x^3 + 2x^2 y,$ what is the value of $x$?
task_context.reference_solution: Notice that we can factor out a $5x$ from each term on the left-hand side to give $5x(x+2y)$. Similarly, we can factor out an $x^2$ from each term on the right-hand side to give $x^2(x+2y)$. Thus, we have $5x(x+2y) = x^2(x+2y)$. Since $x$ and $y$ are positive, we can safely divide both sides by $x(x+2y),$ which gives $x = \boxed{5}$.

No, because they are positive, so x + 2y must be positive. So I'm left with 5x = x^2. That means x = 5, right? Just tell me yes or no so I can submit!
